papers.title: Effect of Implant Surface and Radiation Dose on Crestal Bone Loss in Irradiated Patients: 1-Year Preliminary Outcomes.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Implant-supported prosthetic rehabilitation is frequently required in head and neck cancer patients but carries an elevated risk of impaired osseointegration and peri-implant bone loss. Hydrophilic implant surfaces have demonstrated improved early osseointegration in preclinical studies. However, clinical evidence, especially in irradiated patients, remains limited. This study aimed to compare short-term clinical and radiologic outcomes of hydrophilic implants versus conventional implants placed in irradiated bone. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this study, 107 implants (conventional surface: n=53; hydrophilic surface: n=54) were placed in 21 irradiated patients with head and neck cancer using a split-mouth design. Panoramic radiographs were obtained at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months, and mesial and distal crestal bone loss was assessed. Further, effects of implant surface and implant-specific radiation dose were evaluated. RESULTS: At 12 months, hydrophilic implants demonstrated significantly reduced crestal bone loss compared with conventional implants both mesially (0.6±0.7 versus 0.9±0.7 mm; P<0.001) and distally (0.5±0.4 versus 0.9±0.6 mm; P<0.001). Implant location and radiation-dose category did not show statistically significant associations with bone loss over time. CONCLUSIONS: Hydrophilic implant surfaces were associated with reduced early crestal bone loss in irradiated patients, while radiation dose exhibited no measurable impact within the first year. This study is the first to demonstrate a potential benefit of hydrophilic implants in irradiated patients, including those with autologous bone grafts. Hydrophilic implants may represent a promising option for implant rehabilitation in this high-risk patient population.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文为头颈癌放疗患者牙种植体的临床影像随访，与增材制造多孔植入物、应力遮挡或LPBF力学测试无关。
llm.why_not_core: This is a clinical split-mouth radiographic study of dental implant surface hydrophilicity in irradiated patients, with no LPBF fabrication, no porous structure design, no stress shielding or stiffness matching analysis, and no mechanical or fatigue testing.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估亲水表面种植体在放疗患者中能否改善早期骨结合。
summary_zh.method: 21例放疗患者采用分口设计植入107枚种植体，随访12个月全景片测量边缘骨吸收。
summary_zh.result: 亲水种植体近远中骨吸收均显著低于常规表面，放疗剂量无显著影响。

summary_en.motivation: The study addresses whether hydrophilic implant surfaces can mitigate the elevated risk of impaired osseointegration and peri-implant bone loss in irradiated head and neck cancer patients.
summary_en.method: In a split-mouth design, 107 conventional and hydrophilic implants were placed in 21 irradiated patients, and mesial and distal crestal bone loss was measured on panoramic radiographs at baseline, 6, and 12 months.
summary_en.result: Hydrophilic implants showed significantly less crestal bone loss than conventional implants at 12 months, whereas implant location and radiation-dose category were not significantly associated with bone loss.
summary_en.validation: Clinical radiographic follow-up of human patients over one year.
